away.name: Ville Husso
away.news: Husso has seen limited action this season, but he will start again in the front end of a back-to-back, his second start in eight games. That said, Husso has been solid when called upon, posting a 1.58 GAA and .935 SV% in two appearances (1-0-0). The 31-year-old Finnish goalie earned a backup role with the Ducks in 2025-26 after spending most of the previous two seasons in the AHL. The Ducks enter Monday's contest as +135 road underdogs against a New York Rangers team that has been outscored 8-1 in their last two games (0-1-1).

home.name: Dylan Garand
home.news: Garand had a forgetful performance last week, allowing four goals on 13 shots (.692 SV%) in a 7-1 loss to the New Jersey Devils, but bounced back in his following outing, saving 28 of 29 shots (.966 SV%) in a 1-0 overtime loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets. Despite his poor outing last week, Garand has filled in admirably for Igor Shesterkin after his season-ending injury, posting a 1.82 GAA and .927 SV% in six games (3-2-1). The Rangers enter Monday's contest as -139 home favourites against an Anaheim Ducks team on a two-game losing streak (0-2-0).

away.name: Mackenzie Blackwood
away.news: Despite some inconsistent play from Blackwood, Colorado will continue to roll with him as their go-to goalie early in the 2026-27 season, turning to him for the seventh time in their first nine games. Inconsistencies aside, Blackwood has played well in his last two games (2-0-0), saving 54 of 58 shots (.931 SV%). He has a 2.86 GAA and .891 SV% in six games (4-2-0). The Avalanche enter Monday's contest as significant -236 road favourites against a struggling Philadelphia Flyers team that has scored only 14 goals in its first 10 games (1-6-3).

home.name: Joseph Woll
home.news: After their first win of a disappointing 2026-27 season (1-6-3), the Flyers will flip the script and turn to Joseph Woll on Monday. Dan Vladar's win aside, Woll has been the Flyers' far more reliable goalie this season, posting a 2.77 GAA and .916 SV% in five games (0-3-2). He came up just short in his most recent outing, saving 24 of 26 shots (.923 SV%), but lacked goal support, a frequent occurrence this season, in a 2-1 loss to the Detroit Red Wings. The Flyers enter Monday's contest as sizeable +204 home underdogs against a Colorado Avalanche team that has outscored opponents 36-24 over eight games (5-2-1).

away.name: Yaroslav Askarov
away.news: The Sharks are off to a modest 4-3-1 start to the season, but Askarov's quality goaltending has been few and far between, leaving little room for error. Askarov has allowed three or more goals in every outing this season, including five on 25 shots (.800 SV%) in his most recent game, a 6-3 loss to the Boston Bruins. The 24-year-old goalie has an ugly 3.99 GAA and .848 SV% in five games (2-3-0). The Sharks enter Monday's contest as +114 road underdogs against a Toronto Maple Leafs team on a three-game losing streak (0-1-2).

home.name: Sergei Bobrovsky
home.news: The Maple Leafs hoped Bobrovsky's poor 2025-26 season with the Florida Panthers was an anomaly, but his start to the 2026-27 season hasn't been encouraging. The veteran 38-year-old goalie has an ugly 3.29 GAA and .891 SV%, winning only one of six games (1-3-2). He has allowed three or more goals in each game this season. The Maple Leafs enter Monday's contest as -127 home favourites against a 4-3-1 San Jose Sharks team.

away.name: Arturs Silovs
away.news: The Penguins are in a three-game losing streak (0-3-0) and hope to return to the win column on Monday, turning to Silovs to tend the twine against the Utah Mammoth. The 25-year-old Latvian goalie started the season with a 19-save shutout in a 7-0 win over the Philadelphia Flyers, but he has struggled since, allowing five goals in three of four games (2-2-0) and posting a 4.00 GAA and .853 SV%. The Penguins enter Friday's contest as +164 road underdogs against a 6-3-0 Mammoth team.

home.name: Sebastian Cossa
home.news: Over the weekend, Utah's Head Coach André Tourigny indicated he wanted a more even goalie rotation, and he is acting on it immediately by turning to Cossa to tend the twine on Monday. The 23-year-old Cossa was excellent in his season debut, saving 18 of 19 shots (.947 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets, but has struggled in two outings since, allowing four goals on 12 shots (.667 SV%). The Mammoth enter Monday's action as -183 home favourites against a Pittsburgh Penguins team that has been outscored 16-7 during a three-game losing streak (0-3-0).
